Welcome to Voat! So what's a mechanical keyboard? I'm imagining a vintage typewriter.

Thats quite the topic. So mechanical keyboards are keyboards that have mechanical keys. Typically most keyboards have started using rubber-domes to create the click of each key. This is led to a very mushy typing experience. There are other boards however that use real switches for each key, these switches typically have some sort of spring under-neither each key. There are many variations based on personal preference however, such as how hard the key is to press, if they make a clicky noise when pressed, if there is no noise just a bump when pressed. Another benefit is the keys do not need to be pressed all the way down to trigger. This helps with finger fatigue and can help increase typing speed. I would defiantly check out some keyboards in the /v/keyboards. Here's a link to my current keyboard - My Baby
